newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: First Chicago trades exotics in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago trades exotics in Singapore.

text.p: The United States' ninth largest bank First Chicago NBD Corp opened a branch in Singapore on Monday and promptly did its first Asian-based deal in Southeast Asian regional currencies, officials said.
First Chicago's Asia Pacific senior vice president Peter McCarthy told reporters at a briefing the bank had started its foreign exchange dealings in Asian exotic currencies immediately.
Of the 20 staff the bank employs in the city-state, 18 were concerned with foreign exchange, he said.
"We did out first deal at 8.15 this morning" (0015 GMT), he said.
First Chicago's head of Southeast Asian operations, Paul McGonagle, said he expected at least half of the bank's business to be in foreign exchange trading with the rest in corporate banking.
About half of the foreign exchange activities would be proprietorial, he said.

Under its newly-issued offshore banking licence, the bank will be allowed to trade up to US$250 million in non-Singapore dollar currencies and lend Singapore $150 million from its Singapore base, he said.
"We will risk manage all the bank's ASEAN currency operations from this office," McGonagle said. "We will also be marketing G7 (currency) products here but those will be risk managed elsewhere."
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
G7 groups Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.

First Chicago's executive vice president for corporate and institutional banking, Philip Jones, said the trade in Southeast Asian currencies was growing rapidly as more and more American and European companies increased their business in the region.
"So many companies are doing more and more business here and that is dramatically increasing currency flows," Jones said.
